lines.say: The Legend of Zelda was inspired by a kid exploring the countryside.
It came out in Japan in 1986, and in America in 1987, in a shiny gold cartridge.
Shigeru Miyamoto based it on his childhood, hiking the woods and stumbling onto a hidden lake.
It was one of the first games with a battery inside the cartridge, so you could save your adventure.
Beat it, and you unlock a harder Second Quest, with new dungeons.
And Princess Zelda is named after Zelda Fitzgerald, the wife of author F. Scott Fitzgerald.
Did you beat the Second Quest? Follow for more 8-Bit Backstory!
